beats.text: Boethius had it all — wealth, honour, the ear of an emperor. Then it collapsed overnight.
Falsely accused, he sat in a cell awaiting execution, raging at how unfair it all was.
There, he imagined Philosophy herself appearing to reason with him about Fortune.
Fortune turns a wheel, she says. It lifts you high — but turning is the only thing it ever promised.
Everything she gave was a loan, never a gift. To weep when it's recalled is to misunderstand the deal.
So cling to nothing that the wheel can reach. Build your peace on what Fortune cannot touch.
He wrote this consolation while awaiting death — and found, at the bottom of the wheel, a strange calm.

source_note: From The Consolation of Philosophy (public-domain translation) — paraphrased.
